extracted.intended_audience: medical/microbiology laboratory students and practising bacteriologists
extracted.subtask_description: Laboratory protocols and evaluative criteria for examining bacterial growth and development under physical conditions (atmosphere, temperature, medium reaction, lethal agents) and for assessing pathogenicity and toxin activity in experimental animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atmosphere (oxygen requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the organism is an obligate aerobe, facultative anaerobe, or obligate anaerobe and examine behaviour in the absence of oxygen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial inference from fermentation tubes (growth in closed branch, bulb, inverted gas tube vs bulk). For accurate assessment, prepare sets of cultivations on glucose formate media incubated aerobically and anaerobically, seal sets in Buchner's tubes or Bulloch's apparatus, exhaust air with a pump and absorb residual oxygen with pyrogallic acid and caustic soda. Observe macroscopically and microscopically at 24-hour intervals for up to seven days and control results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gases other than oxygen
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess organism survival and death when exposed to specific non-oxygen gases (e.g., SO2, N2O, NO, CO2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Bulloch's apparatus with a sterile gas filter and connect to a gasometer or generator. Replace air in the bell jar with the test gas (confirm by analysing exit samples), incubate at optimum temperature, remove one tube daily and, if no growth, incubate under optimum conditions to determine exposure length required to kill the organism. Control results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperature — Range
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the range of temperatures at which the organism grows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a series of ten tube cultivations in fluid media of optimum reaction. Arrange incubators at fixed temperatures varying by 5°C between about 5°C and 50°C (or use water-bath). Incubate one cultivation per incubator (aerobic or anaerobic as needed), examine at half-hour intervals for 5–18 hours, note temperature at first macroscopic growth (optimum) and continue up to seven days to note extremes. Control results; if necessary refine to each degree around extremes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperature — Optimum
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix the precise optimum growth temperature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a second series of ten tube cultivations and incubate in temperatures at 1°C intervals for five degrees on either side of previously observed optimum; observe at half-hour intervals and note temperature at which growth is first visible to the naked eye as the optimum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermal death-point — Moist (Vegetative forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Thermal death-point defined as the temperature which with certainty kills a watery suspension of vegetative organisms after an exposure of 10 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a special water-bath regulated to 0.5°C intervals (approx. 50–80°C), sterile capsules, saline, calibrated pipettes, special platinum loop, thin glass test-tubes. Prepare twelve suspensions from 48-hour solid media, expose successive tubes to increasing fixed temperatures (start at 40°C, increase by 2°C steps), each for ten minutes with rapid cooling, pour plates and flask cultures, incubate and observe up to seven days; the lowest temperature causing no growth after seven days is the t.d.p. For greater accuracy repeat with 0.5°C steps around observed point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermal death-point — Moist (Spores)
rubrics_metrics.description: For spores, thermal death-point is the time of exposure at a fixed 100°C necessary to kill all spores in a suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce spore-containing cultures; emulsify surface growth into saline, place in fitted Erlenmeyer flask and subject to boiling water-bath/steam can system with syphon sampling. When flask reaches 100°C, discard first cc syphoned, collect next 5 c.c. at intervals (e.g., every 25 minutes) and prepare plates and flasks; observe up to seven days. For finer timing, sample at 0.5–1 minute intervals in the critical period before previously determined death-point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermal death-point — Dry (Vegetative forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Thermal death-point for a thin dry film of vegetative organisms is the temperature that kills them with certainty after a 10-minute exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make thin films on sterile cover-slips, dry, place in sterile capsules, expose each to different fixed temperatures in a hot-air oven for ten minutes (varying by 5°C between 60°C and 120°C), remove immediately, transfer film to nutrient bouillon, prepare subcultures from flasks showing growth to rule out contamination, and control results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermal death-point — Dry (Spores)
rubrics_metrics.description: Thermal death-point for spores in a thin dry film: temperature which with certainty kills spores after a 10-minute exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare spore-rich sloped agar cultures, emulsify growth and spread thin films on cover-slips, expose each for ten minutes at temperatures varying by 5°C between 100°C and 160°C in a hot-air oven, then proceed as for vegetative forms with incubation and controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reaction of medium — Range
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the range of medium reaction (pH) permitting macroscopic growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a bouillon culture, dilute 1:100, inoculate a series of nutrient bouillon tubes with reactions ranging from +25 to -30 (steps of 5). Observe half-hourly from 3rd to 12th hour to note tubes where macroscopic growth first appears (probable optimum), continue up to seven days to note extremes. Control the observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reaction of medium — Optimum reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Refine the optimum pH/reaction of the medium within narrower limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on the range experiment, inoculate tubes with smaller reaction increments (e.g., steps of 1 unit) for five points on either side of previously observed optimum and observe as before to fix optimum reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resistance to desiccation
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure organism survival under drying conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Mueller's desiccator with concentrated sulphuric acid and an exhaust pump, prepare thin films from a 48-hour surface culture (ensure absence of spores), dry films in ventilated Petri dishes, place in desiccator, exhaust and admit dry sterile air. At intervals (e.g., every five hours) remove a film, transfer to nutrient bouillon and incubate up to seven days to determine death time; pour plates from growing flasks to check contamination and repeat around the determined death time with finer intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resistance to light (diffuse, direct, colours)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess bactericidal effect of diffuse daylight, direct sunlight, and specific spectral colours on plated cultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare plate cultivations (agar and gelatine) from a bouillon culture; set controls in incubators. For diffuse light, cover part of plates with a black paper star/cross, expose unprotected portions to diffuse daylight for varying hours (1–12+), then incubate and compare with controls up to seven days. For direct sunlight, place plates in sun with dishes of 2% potash alum solution to absorb heat. For primary colours, coat covers with collodion containing aniline dyes (chrysoidin, malachite green, eosin, methyl violet), expose to bright daylight (not direct sun) for varying periods, incubate and compare. Note that bactericidal action is strongest with violet/UV rays; UV from mercury vapour lamps is especially destructive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resistance to heat
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess heat sensitivity; see thermal death-point protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to thermal death-point experiments for moist and dry conditions and for vegetative forms and spores; use appropriate water-bath or hot-air oven apparatus and the stepwise exposure and incubation procedures described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resistance to antiseptics and disinfectants — overall approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate bacterial resistance to chemical germicides with respect to inhibition, killing of vegetative forms, and killing of spores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess three main points: (A) Inhibition coefficient — percentage of disinfectant preventing growth in nutrient medium; (B) Inferior lethal coefficient — time to kill vegetative forms in water at 20–25°C with medium concentration disinfectant; (C) Superior lethal coefficient — time to kill spores under similar conditions. Use serial dilutions, controlled incubations, and subcultivation to confirm survival vs contamination. Examples: bichloride of mercury, formaldehyde, carbolic acid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inhibition coefficient (disinfectant concentration preventing growth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the percentage (concentration) of disinfectant in the medium sufficient to prevent growth and multiplication of the bacterium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inoculate numbered bouillon tubes and immediately add varying quantities of disinfectant solutions to produce a series of concentrations (examples given for carbolic acid, mercuric perchloride, formaldehyde). Incubate under optimum conditions, examine daily up to seven days, and from tubes showing growth prepare subcultures to verify the organism is the original test organism and not contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inferior lethal coefficient (time to kill vegetative forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the exposure time necessary to kill vegetative forms in water at ~18–25°C when disinfectant is present at a medium concentration (non-plasmolysing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare hanging-drop preparations to determine the strongest non-plasmolysing and weakest plasmolysing solutions, select percentage to test, prepare diluted suspensions in sterile water, distribute into test-tubes with disinfectant, incubate at ~18–20°C, remove at hourly intervals and subculture both control and test suspensions onto nutrient agar, incubate and observe up to seven days to determine shortest lethal exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superior lethal coefficient (time to kill spores)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the exposure time necessary to kill spores under conditions similar to the inferior lethal coefficient test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce abundant spores in surface cultures, heat to destroy vegetative forms (e.g., 80°C for ten minutes), then employ the previously determined disinfectant percentage and follow inferior lethal coefficient procedure (steps 7–14) with adjusted longer intervals (2–5 hours if needed). Observe and control results up to seven days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutralization/removal of disinfectant traces before subculture
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure traces of disinfectant are removed before transferring to fresh media to avoid false 'no growth' results due to residual germicide rather than organism death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended procedure: add disinfectant to bacterial suspension for required contact time, centrifuge thoroughly and pipette off supernatant, wash deposit with sterile water and repeat centrifugation, resuspend and make up to volume, filter suspension through sterile porcelain candle, emulsify residue with sterile bouillon and prepare subcultures. Alternatively neutralise chemically (e.g., ammonium sulphide for mercurial salts) where appropriate. Determine inhibition coefficient first to guide dilution for subculture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pathogenesis testing (living bacteria) — psychrophilic organisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Test pathogenicity of psychrophilic bacteria (grow only at or below ~18–20°C) in amphibian models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare nutrient broth cultures, incubate seven days, inject culture amount equivalent to 1% body-weight of a healthy frog into the dorsal lymph sac, observe until death or up to 28 days, and perform careful post-mortem if death occurs. Repeat as necessary and test other animals if initial results negative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pathogenesis testing (living bacteria) — mesophilic organisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Test pathogenicity of mesophilic bacteria (grow at ~35–37°C) in small mammal models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare broth cultures incubated 48 hours, select matched mice, inoculate one subcutaneously (root of tail) and another intraperitoneally with amount equal to 1% body-weight, observe until death or up to 28 days, perform post-mortem and repeat inoculations if death occurs; if negative, test other species (rat, guinea-pig, rabbit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal lethal dose (m.l.d.) determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate the smallest dose of culture that causes infection and death in an experimental animal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a calibrated platinum loop of known deposit; prepare series of serial tenfold dilutions (capsules I–IV produce 0.1, 0.001, 0.00001, 0.0000001 loop per c.c.), prepare graded doses and inoculate animals from smallest to largest dose, plate higher dilutions to enumerate organisms and calculate organisms per loopful, and record the smallest dose causing fatal infection as the m.l.d.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toxins — Intracellular/insoluble toxins (killed-culture testing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Test for toxicity of intracellular/insoluble toxins present in killed cultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare long-term glucose formate broth cultures (e.g., 14 days), heat fluid culture at 60°C for 30 minutes (killed culture), inoculate a control tube of bouillon to confirm sterility, inject animals intravenously with volume equal to 1% body-weight, observe up to 28 days, perform post-mortem on fatalities, repeat experiments at least once, and, if positive, estimate minimal lethal dose of killed culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toxins — Extracellular/soluble toxins (filtered-toxin testing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Test for toxicity of soluble extracellular toxins present in cell-free filtrates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filter culture through a porcelain (Berkefeld) filter into a sterile flask, inoculate animals subcutaneously with quantity equal to 1% body-weight and observe up to one month, inoculate a control broth tube to confirm filtrate sterility, perform complete post-mortems on fatalities and repeat as needed.
